sections.text: Response Letter Status Submitted to State Response Letter Date 03/16/2026 Submitted Date 03/16/2026 Dear Mark Reese, Introduction: Thank you for your recent correspondence.  See the responses to the objections you included in the pdf "NYLM - Infirmity Objection" below.

sections.heading: Response 1
sections.text: Comments: SERFF Tracking #: NYLM-134614243 State Tracking #: MR NYLM-134614243 Company Tracking #: G-31272-0 ASM 10YLT SINGLE CASE FILING State: Montana Filing Company: New York Life Insurance Company TOI/Sub-TOI: L04G Group Life - Term/L04G.103 Renewable - Single Life - Fixed/Indeterminate Premium Product Name: G-31272-0 ASM 10YLT SINGLE CASE FILING Project Name/Number: G-31272-0 ASM 10YLT SINGLE CASE FILING/G-31272-0 ASM 10YLT SINGLE CASE FILING PDF Pipeline for SERFF Tracking Number NYLM-134614243 Generated 08/18/2026 09:00 PM Comments: NYL - Infirmity Objection: If an elderly person with mobility problems or vertigo falls, and the fall causes an aneurysm, which then causes death. Would this be covered by the policy? NYLM Response: See Covered Loss and What Benefit is Payable in the AD&D Insurance page(s). In the company example: A person with heart disease falls and dies. The company then states the fall alone did not cause death; the heart condition contributed and the accident would be not covered by the policy. If the coverage is excluded, is it excluded because the heart disease contributed to the fall or because it contributed to the death, or both? Please further explain. NYLM Response: See the For The Benefit To Be Paid in the AD&D Insurance page(s). Would the policy provide coverage if an insured dies because they accidentally took too much of their high blood pressure medicine or if they are overprescribed the high blood pressure medicine? NYLM Response: See Self-Inflicted Injury/Suicide in the AD&D Insurance page(s). The Certificate does not define what constitutes a covered accident. Why doesnt the company define accident and provide clear examples of accidents that are covered and accidents that are not covered in the Certificate itself? For example: the person with heart disease who falls and later dies versus a healthy person who slips on the ice, hits their head and the result is death. NYLM Response: In reviewing the referenced case, it appears that it is pertaining to an AD&D voluntary policy, which differs from this filing. This policy is a Life/AD&D product filed under the TOI:L04G Group Life  Term which seems to be outside of the scope of the referenced case.  Could you please provide the specific Montana statutes you are referencing regarding the definition of "accident" as it relates to discretionary group policies? For additional clarification regarding this filing, you can refer to the "Covered Loss" section on the AD&D Insurance pages as well as the Accidental Death & Dismemberment Insurance Schedule, which outlines how the benefit is paid. The Certificate does not define what constitutes a covered accident. NYLM Response: See the "Covered Loss" section on the AD&D Insurance pages. Additionally, the Montana Supreme Court held: Life Ins. Co. v. Evans, 195 Mont 242, 247 (1981) Where an accidental injury aggravates or triggers a pre-existing dormant disease or physical infirmity, the accident may be said to have been the proximate cause of the resulting disability within the terms and meaning of an ordinary accident insurance policy. The mere presence of a pre-existing disease or infirmity will no longer relieve the insurer from liability in this state. Recovery may be had even though the disease appears to have actually contributed to the cause of death as long as the accident sets in motion the chain of events leading to death, or if it is the prime or moving cause.
